### Added
- **`install.sh --global` (`install.ps1 -Global`) installs from a release bundle for the whole machine.** The engine is copied to `~/.local/share/harness/<version>` (XDG), `current` points at it and the repo is wired to `<home>/current` -- `harness setup` with the bundle as its source, then `harness doctor`. `--pin` wires the version dir. Before, `--global` was an unknown flag and a piped install was always per project.
- **The harness runs a TypeScript repo's tests, type check, lint and coverage itself, and the gate owes them by name.** Test runners are rows of the language book (`languages.<id>.runners`): pytest, and vitest and jest with `executor: harness` — `hs-code test run --targets|--changed|--all` calls them through `node_modules/.bin` (never a package manager), from the directory that owns their config, and reads the verdict from the result file, never the exit code. A repo declares static checks in `codemap.yaml` `languages.typescript.checks` (`tsc -b`, `eslint`), run by `hs-code check run` against a baseline the harness keeps (`--freeze`, `--shrink`, `--rebuild-baseline` on a tool major change with an approver and a new DEC): a finding past the baseline fails, a config error the tool names (TS5101) is BROKEN, a run that would write over uncommitted work is refused before it starts and put back if it did. `codemap.yaml` `coverage:` sets line floors per map group, judged on `test run --all --coverage`. Strictness is the stricter of the plan's base and HEAD. A declared check is owed by name, for everything the plan changed since its base (committed or not): `hs-run cook next` routes the exact command (`needs_declared_check`) and the DoD gate accepts only a result the harness wrote — the newest row of the phase's check ledger must match the file, the tree it ran on (a test run reads every file under its units; tsc also reads `.json`), the spec it ran under and a mode no laxer than the one owed now; a run whose inputs moved under it is BLOCKED, naming each file and telling one that changed while it ran from one it wrote; a runner is proven only by a run over every test. Each line records the plan base it was held to, and marks moved past a recorded base or a verified commit are refused; the policy is read at the base and at the marks' point (never at a state inside a phase), the strictest per check (the earlier on a tie), so a commit named by `cook verify --sha` moves what is owed back and never the floor down; a plan whose marks are gone while a run's traces remain (`harness-runs/`, a ledger run, a verification naming its commits) takes no new mark (re-pin with a DEC). The ledger and the marks are caged against shell writes and the common shell removals (globs, `bash -c`, `xargs` fed by a pipeline that names or `find`s them, `rsync --delete`/`--del`, `git clean` with or without a pathspec, `git -C <dir> rm`, a `git -c alias.*`, a `find` from `$PWD` or under a `cd` included), each command read the way the shell runs it -- quotes removed, inside `( )`/`{ }`/`if`/`$( )`/`bash -c`, past `timeout 5`/`nice -n 5`/ `env -i`, every `cd` followed through `&&`/`||`; under a `cd` no reading can follow, only the names the cage holds (each gate kind as `.yaml` or `.json`) are refused. `find . -name '*.ts' -not -path './node_modules/*'` goes through; `rm -f $(find …)`, `rm "$f"` are judged by what they may point at. A TS-only repo is detected and adopted (`hs-code graph init`, the codemap offer), and a repo's `packageManager` field (`pnpm@10.4.1`) names its package manager. Closes BL-359..362 (`plans/261019-1326-language-packs-typescript-m2a`). What the ledger does not stop: `docs/harness/config-reference.md`.
- **A cross-plan edge can be waived by a ruling.** `{from: <plan>/<phase>, to: <phase>, waived: {decision, reason}}` in the waiting plan's `plan-graph.yaml` says the edge is met before the other plan's phase passed (its in-repo half merged, the rest waits on something outside). Before, the waiting phase and every phase after it stayed blocked until the other phase passed in full. `cook next` hands the phase out, and `cook next` and `cook close` name the waiver and its decision while the other phase has not passed; the other plan still owes that phase. Both keys are required, and a waiver on an edge inside one plan is refused. The waiver is part of the approved plan, so writing one drifts the approval.
- **hs-code reads TypeScript/JavaScript through language packs.** The code map's kernel keeps the shape (records, edges, units, snapshots) and a pack keeps the meaning: which files are its own, the reader that parses one, the resolver that names modules and classifies imports. Packs are rows of `harness/data/hs-code-languages.yaml` (which replaces `hs-code-adapters.yaml`): `python`, unchanged byte for byte, and `typescript` (`.ts .tsx .mts .cts .d.ts .js .jsx .mjs .cjs`, pnpm/npm/yarn workspaces). A repo opts in with `codemap.yaml` `languages: {typescript: {engine: tree-sitter|typescript}}`. The engine must be named and is never switched by machine. `tree-sitter` needs two optional wheels. `typescript` runs a harness-pinned TypeScript 6.0.3 in one Node process per snapshot, installed once per user under `~/.local/share/harness/lang-tools/` by `hs-code init run --apply --only lang-tools`. An engine missing what it needs refuses with exit 3 and the install line, for the interpreter that lacks it. The refusal never falls back to the other engine. A TS module is its repo path. Imports resolve through relative paths, workspace package names, `exports` subpaths, tsconfig `paths` and Vite/webpack aliases. Each lands in `imports_module_level` / `_function_local` / `_type_only` / `_external` or `imports_unresolved` with a reason code. `*.test.*`/`*.spec.*`/`__tests__` are `role: test` and `*.stories.*` are `role: story`. A story shows under `stories` in `change test select` and `code.tests_reached` and is never selected. `graph where|importers [--symbol]|tests|drift` and `change structural` read TS modules. An edge into another workspace package carries `import_flags` (`declared: own:<field> | ancestor:… | types_only | undeclared`). The new rule kind `package_boundary` turns them into violations, and `layer_direction` counts `import type` edges as `type_only`.
- **A project's own resolver over one batched command.** A `codemap.yaml` `adapters:` row that names a `resolver:` beside its `command:` is a whole language: path ids under `lang: <id>`, every import answered by the resolver over `hs-code-resolve/1`, one process per snapshot pass, every answer checked. The `typescript` pack takes the same protocol as `languages.typescript.resolver_command`, asked first for each bare specifier, and `defer` hands the specifier back.
### Changed
- **The release preflight runs its CI on the homelab.** Every job `scripts/ci_local.sh` dispatches runs on the host `.rops.env` names, one `hs-rops` cell per job on the `release` lane, at the clean commit about to be cut; only `ci_local.sh --local-only` (its diff-vs-`main` steps, which a lane cannot run) stays on the dev box. A host not configured or not answering stops the cut and names `--ci local`; `release/release.yaml` `ci:` sets the default. The tree is checked clean before any CI (DEC-v-hieubt15-358).
- **Trust covers a project's commands as they were when trusted.** `hs-cli trust` now records a fingerprint of every command `codemap.yaml` declares, covering the argv and the bytes of each in-repo script it runs, and prints them. A command edited since (including by a `git pull`) refuses with exit 3, naming both fingerprints. A bare program name that PATH finds as a file of the repo's own source refuses too: name it by its path so its bytes are fingerprinted (a tool installed where git ignores it, such as a `.venv`, runs as an installed tool). A trust store written before fingerprints existed trusts no command, so **a repo with an `adapters:` reader must run `hs-cli trust <repo>` once after upgrading**.
- **Snapshot schema and file caps.** A snapshot holding a non-Python record is written at `schema_version: 3`, and a Python-only snapshot keeps `2`. `max_file_bytes` (default 1 MiB) caps TS files. Python files get a cap only when `languages.python.max_file_bytes` sets one.
- **Rule kinds and verbs name the languages they read.** `register_kind(..., languages=)` is required, and a pack outside the bin that registers a kind must declare it. A Python-only kind meeting another language's modules is red with `language_unsupported`. A Python-only verb given another language's target refuses with exit 3, naming it. This covers the project's own languages too.
- **CI's `hs-code` job installs Node and the pinned TypeScript** so both engines' tests run.
- **`hs-run cook open --reason` reopens a completed plan.** Before, a plan whose evidence went stale after close had no way back: `open` started only pending or approved plans and `close` finished only in_progress ones. Reopening runs the same approval gate `open` runs, appends a `reopen` line (reason, phases, actor, ts) to the plan's phase-commits log, moves every `review-decision` aside to `review-decision-retired-<ts>.<ext>`, retires its `record code-reviewer` line, and flips completed to in_progress. A fresh recorded review is then owed, and no measured waiver stands in for it. Each phase named with `--phase` must be verified again: `cook next` answers `needs_reopen_verify`, `cook close` refuses with `reopen_verify_owed`, and the pr/merge/ship/deploy gate refuses too, until a verify of that phase follows the reopen. The auto-finalize no longer closes a reopened plan; `cook close` does.
- **`cook verify --sha keep`** names the commits the phase's last verify recorded.
- **`yaml_comment_cut_nudge` names a YAML value a ` #` cut short.** YAML starts a comment at any ` #` outside quotes, so `title: kept here (see issue #67)` loads as `kept here (see issue` with no error, and a page rendered from the file keeps the cut. After a Write/Edit/MultiEdit to a `.yaml`/`.yml` file, the nudge names each cut that call made (against the prior text the tool result carries): a value whose comment, on the same line, closes a bracket the value opened, or whose glued `#` breaks prose mid-sentence, two words or more on each side. A one-token note after a complete value (`optimizer: Adam #Momentum`) is left alone. It never blocks. `scripts/yaml_comment_cut.py FILE...` answers the same question for a file written any other way (exit 1 on a cut; 2 when a file cannot be read, or a line holding a ` #` could not be scanned). A character YAML does not allow is read as a space; where ruamel's scanner rejects a line, as it does `[mat:loader]`, scanning resumes past it and the deeper lines that can only go on with what it opened (from the first line the scanner had not handed out a token for, as deep as a flow collection still open there; a plain key whose `:` never came is marked on the next line, which is read). A skipped line with a ` #` after a value is reported unread, and the nudge names the ones the call made unread, every copy when one is copied; a cut in a line that was unread before the edit is not blamed on it.

### Fixed
- **A bundle install keeps its launchers executable.** `release/pack.py` packed every file `0o644`, so `harness/bin/hs-code` (and every `hs-*` launcher, and the `--cli` shims pointing at them) answered `Permission denied` after an install from a bundle. A member's mode now comes from git's index (`100755` ships `0o755`); the tarball stays byte-reproducible.
- **`cook next` takes no mark in a tree off the plan's branch.** Run in the main checkout while the plan's declared branch was checked out in a linked worktree, it appended an `open` line for the main checkout, and the plan's base is read from those lines. Now, unless `--phase` claims it, such a tree takes no mark and is told which worktree holds the branch. A tree whose HEAD holds the branch's tip is its home too, judged by ancestry.
- **A stopped `hs-rops run` takes its far run down and frees its seats.** A supervisor stopping a background run sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL about 1.4 s later; the client died, its `ssh` lived on in a session of its own, and the far run kept its pool seats. On SIGTERM, SIGHUP or Ctrl-C both lanes start a reaper the SIGKILL cannot reach, which kills the group stamped beside the run's log -- every host's, for a `--hosts` fan-out; a signal the client was started ignoring (`nohup`) stays ignored. `hs-rops lock status` names each run's group and, for a holder, the `hs-rops kill <pgid>` that frees it.
- **A `post:` artifact is found under the name its writer gives it.** `hs:plan` writes `post: [verification-<node>.json, review-decision.json]` while `write_review_decision.py` writes `review-decision.yaml`, the spelling the gate reads first; `cook next` then sat at `phase_needs_post_artifact` "missing review-decision.json" for good, and the cage leaves no shell route to a `.json`. A post entry naming an artifact kind (`review-decision`, `.yaml` or `.json`) is now read the way the gate reads that kind.
- **A dir removed locally leaves the lane whole.** An exclude protected the far copy from `--delete`, so after a dist rename the old dir stayed on the lane holding only `__pycache__/`, an importable namespace package. The shared excludes on a push (`lane`, `sync --delete`) are perishable; a kept name (`ROPS_LANE_KEEP`, with or without a trailing `/`) is the lane's own directory at its root, protected on both, while a source directory of the same name deeper in the tree (`app/logs/`) is carried like any other; `sync --back` keeps plain excludes.
- **`hs-rops run --label` takes any text, and `run`/`bench` take their command only after `--`.** A label with a space (`--label "full suite + mypy"`) broke the remote line: the label named the log file, and that path reaches the far shell unquoted. The file name now keeps only shell-safe characters, and the queue still shows the label as typed. A stray word after a flag (`--lock x ly do`, meant as a reason) used to become the command and run. It is now refused with exit 2, naming `--`. An alias's extra arguments (`hs-rops test -k foo`) are unchanged.
- **A critique's disposition table is read for its cites.** Only `## Red-team disposition` tables were read, so a `## Critique disposition (r2)` table beside them was left out without a word: on one real plan its 57 cites were neither checked nor moved, and `disposition_cites` still said 84 of 85 matched. Every `## <lens> disposition` table is now read, checked and rewritten by `--pin-cites`/`--remap-cites`; a red-team REVISE is still answered only by red-team tables (DEC-v-hieubt15-344). A heading that mentions a disposition, has a table under it and is not read (another level, `dispositions`, no lens, setext, a table under a sub-heading) is named with its line on `hs-run plan next`. Front matter, code blocks and HTML blocks are found by a CommonMark parser and skipped when cites are checked or rewritten, in a section body or a pointed-to file as well; a disposition table inside one is named. The gate never trusts that skipping alone: it also reads the plan line by line as before, an empty cell either reading finds holds the plan, a finding is answered only by a row both find, and a red-team heading only inside a block holds it with its line named — fuzzed over 50,000 plans, it holds wherever the earlier gate held. A red-team heading glued to its suffix (`disposition_r2`) or written with a Unicode dash is quoted by the gate.
- **`manual_test.py --anchor` keeps the output it captured.** An acceptance run that failed on a peer left only an output hash, so a second probe had to find the 401. The command, exit code, stdout and stderr now go, secrets redacted, to an owner-only file under `telemetry/manual-test-output/` (newest 50 kept, each stream capped at its last 1 MB, only that window redacted), named on the record as `output_file` and printed as `output=`; a run that exits non-zero prints its last 20 lines (at most 4000 chars), and a run that times out names what it printed so far. Nothing is written where no project resolves. `output_hash` is unchanged.
- **`secret_patterns.redact` takes a private key whole and stays linear.** It replaced only the `-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----` line, leaving the key body in the text; it now takes the block to its END line, or the key lines after the header when the END was cut off. The unquoted-secret pattern's digit lookahead rescanned the whole run from every label, so `redact` on untrusted output went quadratic (80k chars of `pwd=`: 7.4 s); the lookahead is now bounded at 256 chars. A JWT no longer starts right after a base64url char, which made a run of `-eyJ` quadratic the same way.
- **`code.callers` decides a method use by the class its receiver evidently has.** `PgDocTypeStore.create` on a peer repo read 0 resolved callers and 105 `.create` uses by name, `PgBatches()` among the receivers. A receiver whose class the file states (`Cls()`, `self`, `x: Cls`, `x = Cls()`), the class named through the file's own imports, is resolved through that class's MRO: a use reaching the subject is a caller carrying its `receivers`; every other use stays listed under `unresolved`, one whose receiver is exactly another class (`Other()`) labelled with the class it `reaches` (measured there: 29 uses by 28 callers, 59 labelled another class, 17 undecided). DEC-v-hieubt15-343.
- **Phases order by their number, not their text.** An 11-phase plan with no edges was visited 1, 10, 11, 2 by cook and listed that way by `cook status`. Phase ids order by the numbers in them wherever the plan graph lists or batches them, and `scaffold.py plan` pads file numbers to the widest one (`phase-01` … `phase-12`) and takes `--first 0` for a phase 0; a rerun that adds phases keeps every phase file already there as it is, and writes only the new ones.
- **A phase file no longer declares a `status:` nothing keeps.** The phase template wrote `status: pending`, nothing wrote it again and nothing read it, so closed plans read every phase "pending", verified ones too. The template writes none, the planner reference says a phase's state is derived from its `verification-<phase>.json`, and `hs-run cook status` names each phase file of an older plan that still declares one.
- **`cook verify --help` says `--phase` may accompany `--from`.** It said `--from` came "instead of --phase/--verdict/--check"; `--phase` is cross-checked against the file's `phase` and fills one the file leaves out, while `--verdict/--check/--stage` are refused.
- **`code.callers` names a call or index receiver by what it calls.** An unresolved method use through `super().memo_put(...)` listed its receiver as `)`, and `stores[0].x` as `0]`. A receiver ending in a bracket is now the name before it with the brackets kept and the arguments dropped (`super()`, `stores[]`, `get()[]`; `()` for a bare parenthesised expression), read on its own logical line.
- **`hs-run` no longer calls a run "stuck" when the same file argument holds new input.** Three `cook verify --from rec.json`, each with a different record that each wrote, were told on the third to stop and ask `hs:escalation-consultant`: the streak keyed a call by its verb and argument TEXT only. An argument naming a regular file now adds that file's content digest to the key, so the same path holding another input is another question; the same input three times still escalates.
- **The verification write names a result file the DoD gate would not pass.** A `file` given relative to the repo (`artifacts/r.xml` read as `artifacts/artifacts/r.xml`), missing, unparseable, or with failing tests passed in silence. The write now prints the check and what the gate would read, beside the advisory for checks with no file.
- **A phase snapshot yields to a re-verify that shows the DoD gate strictly more.** `cook verify --check smoke:PASS` (smoke reads as junit; the flag form carries no file) counted the phase and became `verification-<phase>.json`, and the full re-verify with a junit file right after it landed only in phase-latest: the phase's record held no evidence for good, and nothing short of hand-editing replaced it. Now a later counting record replaces the snapshot when every name in it is a known type, it holds a passing result (a result file the gate reads and passes, or a witnessed manual anchor) for every type the snapshot holds one for, and it adds one more type or drops a name the gate cannot see; the old one goes to `phase-superseded-<phase>.jsonl`. A type counts only when every check of it passes, as the gate reads them; the coverage floor and a hard manual check's co-sign belong to the change-class and are not compared. No replacement drops a type the snapshot held a passing result for, so renaming misnamed checks no longer loses one either. The write names each PASS check that carries no result file, since the gate cannot see it. A result `file` or `format` that is not text no longer crashes the gate, the well-formedness check, or the write.
- **`yaml_comment_cut` reads a file past more than 200 rejected lines.** It stopped after 200 resumes: 5666 of 91486 YAML files on one machine (generated snapshots holding hundreds of `[typing::Literal]`, which ruamel rejects) were read only in part. Each resume starts past the last, so the cap is a time budget, now 10000 (the most any of those files needed was 959, at about 0.2 ms each).
- **A `cook verify --sha` refusal of a merged lane's commits says the way out.** A phase cooked in its own worktree and merged `--no-ff` before anyone verified it had every commit off the integration branch's first-parent line; the refusal said only that, and its re-run line was the refused command. When one line holds the named commits, it now says that a phase built in another worktree is verified from a worktree whose HEAD is its newest commit (with the `git worktree add --detach` that makes one), with the exact flags (`--phase`, `--plan` as an absolute, quoted path, `--sha` with the named commits less any merge or another phase's, the ones this phase already kept included), and that a verify here then keeps what that one recorded. A phase keeps the list of its last verify only, so a way out without the kept ones dropped them and sent the next verify round to a refusal on them; the refusal's warnings now name what was kept. When no one line holds them it says no single verify records them, and when git cannot say, it says that. A commit not in HEAD's history is said to need a merge first and the verify run again, with no way out offered for the rest meanwhile, since two verifies would each replace the other's list; one another phase's last verify recorded is named as that phase's. It names no lane: which line built the phase git cannot tell.
- **`cook verify --sha` accepts a commit the phase's own last verify recorded**, even off HEAD's first-parent line. A phase cooked on a lane and merged into an integration branch could not be verified again there: every one of its commits came in through the merge, so all were refused, and leaving `--sha` out gave the phase every commit since its mark. Such a commit is recorded with a warning when it is in HEAD's history; a merged commit the phase never recorded, and a recorded one this branch never merged, are still refused.
- **A refusal on an unresolved data root names the value that failed.** Under a global bin, `HARNESS_DATA_ROOT=<project>` (instead of `<project>/.harness`) was refused as "CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR unset", so the operator went to fix a variable that was never wrong. The write fence, the findings store, `hs-cli gates`, and the code-graph snapshot doors now say which variable failed, with the value to set; a tool that also walked cwd for a project names that cwd.
- **`cook verify` refusing a merged commit says what its own `rev-list` lists.** The refusal named the command that lists a phase's own commits and stopped there; an empty field printed beside it read as its answer, "none", on a line of 99 commits. It now runs that command and gives the count and the newest commits, or says the line has none since the phase's mark.
- **The drawio Python import and class graphs can read a stored codegraph snapshot.** On a declared import root, `pyimports.py` and `pyclasses.py` measured the whole repo on every call (about two minutes on a loaded machine); `--snap REF [--snap-store DIR]` reads a stored snapshot instead, and a pin the door cannot take exits with its reason rather than falling back quietly to the AST scan. Their tests read the run's one shared snapshot, so the class-graph check no longer times out.
- **`mutation_guard` traces its skips again instead of crashing on them.** An `import hook_runtime` inside two late branches of its stop step made the name local to the whole function, so every early skip (no snapshot, no identity) raised UnboundLocalError, swallowed fail-open: 495 crash-log lines and no skip trace. A new scan refuses any shipped function that reads a name above its own import of it.
- **`decision_register --amend` re-anchors a live ruling.** It took only `--title` and `--rationale`, so a ruling whose code landed in more places needed a new superseding id for an anchor-only change. `--affects` and `--executed-by` are amended the same way, inside the register lock with the replaced value on the trail; status, lineage and who ruled stay out of reach.
- **A verification's blast radius is scoped by the phase's own commits.** It was scoped by a diff against the default branch's merge-base, which is empty once the phase's lane has merged, and an empty scope was recorded as `reverseDeps: {}`, read as "nothing depends on this" on a package nine others declare a dependency on. `cook verify` now hands the commits it records (named or computed) to the write, the radius covers the files they touched and names those commits, and it is filled only when the code graph measured at least one file in scope; otherwise it is recorded as unavailable with the reason (no file, none measured, no default branch, a commit outside HEAD's history).

## Verifying what you downloaded

This release ships a **checksum file** (`harness-v<VERSION>.tar.gz.sha256`) and a
**component inventory** (`sbom.json`). That is everything you have to check it with, and
the rest of this page is blunt about what they do and do not tell you.

```bash
sha256sum -c harness-v<VERSION>.tar.gz.sha256
```

That answers exactly **one** question: *is the file you are holding the same file the
checksum was written from.* It catches a truncated download, a bad disk, a corrupted
transfer.

### What it cannot answer

The checksum was produced by the **same run**, at the **same moment**, as the archive.
Anyone who can rewrite the archive can rewrite the checksum to match. It is a
**self-referential** check: it proves the archive is intact, not who built it or from
what source.

Answering that needs a **build provenance attestation** — a signed statement, produced by
the build system itself, recorded in a log that lives **outside** the repository. This
release does **not** carry one.

### Why there is none

GitHub refuses to issue one, verbatim:

> `Failed to persist attestation: Feature not available for user-owned private repositories. To enable this feature, please make this repository public.`

That is a platform rule about **who owns the repository**, not a misconfiguration: the
source repo is currently private and user-owned, and GitHub offers this only for public
repositories or ones owned by an organization.

The signing step was wired into the release pipeline and removed when the platform
refused it — removed outright rather than left failing, because a red step nobody can act
on is worse than none. Every constraint around it still lives in
`harness/tests/test_release_provenance_attestation.py` and comes back intact the moment
the step does.

**The way back:** move the source repo to a GitHub organization, **or** make it public.
Either one is enough; no other code changes.

### What to do meanwhile

- Run `sha256sum -c` to rule out a corrupted download.
- **Read `install.sh` / `install.ps1` yourself before running them.** These are the files
  you execute **first**, usually through `curl <url> | sh` — that is, before you get a
  chance to inspect anything. Download them separately, read them, then run. With no
  provenance attestation, reading them is the only protection left.
- Check `sbom.json` if you need to know which libraries the archive pulls in.

### Glossary

- **checksum (`.sha256`)** — a short string summarising a file's contents, used to detect
  corruption or modification; it says nothing about **who** produced the file.
- **build provenance attestation** — a signed statement, produced by the build system,
  recording *which workflow built this archive, from which commit*. This release has none.
- **SBOM (software bill of materials)** — an inventory of the libraries inside the
  archive with their versions, used to check whether any carries a published
  vulnerability.
- **transparency log** — an append-only, publicly readable log whose entries cannot be
  deleted. It is where an attestation signature is recorded, and the reason such a
  signature cannot be quietly swapped for another.
